newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury denies has made MPC appointments.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury denies has made MPC appointments.

text.p: The UK Treasury has not yet made any of its appointments to the interest rate setting Monetary Policy Committee, a Treasury spokeswoman said.

A story in this morning's edition of The Independent newspaper named London Business School economics professor David Currie, Oxford university economist John Flemming and London School of Economics banking and finance professor Charles Goodhart as committee members subject to last minute hitches.
But the report was "completely inaccurate," the Treasury said.
"We are still looking at lists of names and we will be making an announcement in due course," she said.
The committee will have nine members -- the Bank of England governor, his two deputies, two executive directors from the central bank and four appointees of the Treasury.

One deputy governor position is a new one and no announcement has yet been made whilst the current deputy governor, Howard Davies, is moving to the revamped Securities and Investments Board, so his position will be vacant too.
The interim MPC -- central bank governor Eddie George, Deputy Davies and executive directors Mervyn King and Ian Plenderleith -- will be holding its first meeting on June 6.
